info.name: Adverse Search Service API
info.description:
End-to-end walkthrough of the adverse-search service.

**Read this before running anything.**

1. Start the stack: `pnpm local:up && pnpm local:bootstrap`
2. Start the API: `pnpm dev:api`
3. Issue a key: `pnpm key:issue` — it prints the secret once
4. Put that secret in the `apiKey` environment variable
5. Run the folders in order: Health → Subject → Search → Results

**What you are looking at.** The service runs in mock mode. Every source is a fixture and every record is stamped `mode: "MOCK"`. The shape of every response is real; the content is test data. No request leaves your machine.

**The one thing not to misread.** Three independent fields come back and they must be read together: `execution` (did the job finish), `findingsState` (did we find anything) and `coverage` (did we search everything we said we would). `SUCCEEDED` + `NO_MATCHES_FOUND` + `INCOMPLETE` means the run finished, found nothing, and did not search everything it promised. That is not a clean result.

exec: // Fail early and clearly rather than letting every request 401.
throw new Error('No apiKey set. Run `pnpm key:issue` and paste the secret into the environment.');

item.name: 0 — Health
item.description: No auth needed. Confirms the API is up before you debug an auth problem that is really a stopped process.

request.description: Is the process running? Says nothing about its dependencies.
Can it serve traffic? Checks the dependencies it needs. A 503 here usually means the stack is not bootstrapped.

exec: console.log('Not ready. Try: pnpm local:up && pnpm local:bootstrap');

item.name: 1 — Subject
item.description: Who is being screened. A name is enough (decision D-011); anything more improves identity resolution.

request.description:
`purpose` is required. The service records **why** a person was screened, because that is what limits who may later see the result.

`knownCompanies` is accepted as user-supplied and unverified — it is labelled as such all the way through, never presented as a confirmed association.
Subjects are versioned and immutable. A search pins the exact version it ran against, so a result six months old can still say who it was about at the time.

item.name: 2 — Search
item.description: Start a run. The response is a receipt, not an answer.

header.description: Send the same key twice and you get 200 with the same searchId, not a second search. Use a stable value derived from your own record id in production.

request.description:
Returns **202** and a `searchId`. The run is queued; the worker does the work.

A queued run reports `findings: NOT_EVALUATED`. Rendering that as a result would show someone "nothing found" about a search that has not started.

exec: console.log('This was an idempotent replay — same key, same search.');

request.description:
Run this until `execution` is terminal: `SUCCEEDED`, `PARTIAL`, `FAILED` or `CANCELLED`.

In a Collection Run this request re-runs itself until it settles. The `ETag` header carries the revision if you need to detect a stale read.

exec: // Re-run this request until the run settles. Bounded, so a stuck run does not loop forever.
pm.test('run reached a terminal state', () => pm.expect.fail('Still ' + body.execution + ' after 30 polls. Is the worker running? `pnpm dev:worker`'));

request.description: Scoped to the calling key's tenant. There is no way to ask for another tenant's searches.
Only while it is still running. A finished search stays finished — cancelling is not a way to erase a result.

item.name: 3 — Results
item.description: What the search produced, and what it could not reach.

request.description:
There is deliberately **no endpoint that returns findings alone**.

Read together:
- `findings` — what was found, each with its band, four axis values and rationale
- `coverage` — whether everything promised was searched
- `sourceOutcomes` — what each source did, including what refused us and why
- `rejectedLeads` — candidates deliberately not promoted, with reasons. Evidence of diligence, not noise
- `noMatchStatement` — when there are no findings, what the absence does and does not mean
- `mode` — `MOCK` or `LIVE`

A `band` is not a score. Do not rank, average or threshold it into a number.

exec: // The check that matters. An empty result with incomplete coverage is NOT a clean result.
console.log('NOT a clean result: nothing was found AND not everything was searched.');
console.log('--- This is fixture data. Nothing was fetched from any real source.');

request.description: The company graph, frozen to this run. An officer who resolved only partially attaches no companies — a partial identity match is not an association.

item.name: 4 — Admin
item.description:
Source registry and operational controls. Needs a key with `source_admin`:

`pnpm key:issue --role source_admin --label "postman admin"`

request.description: Breaker state, budget spend and kill switch, per source. This is what an operator watches once anything is live.
What the service can and cannot do in a country, and why. Anything other than SUPPORTED means an empty result is reported as `NOT_ESTABLISHED` rather than as "no findings".
Every source version and its lifecycle state. A source is only usable when a version is ACTIVE.

One person, effective immediately, mid-run. The reason is mandatory and reaches the coverage statement of every run that wanted this source.

Releasing needs a **different** person — see the next request.

Four eyes. With one key this returns **403** — that is the check working, not a bug. Issue a second key to release it:

`pnpm key:issue --role source_admin --label "second approver"`

item.name: 5 — Refusals worth seeing
item.description: The API refusing things correctly is most of what it does. These are worth running once so the behaviour is familiar before it happens in anger.

request.description: An unauthenticated request gets 401 with no detail about what exists.
`purpose` is required. The service will not hold a person's name without a recorded reason for screening them.
Schemas are strict. A misspelled field is rejected rather than silently dropped, so a client typo fails loudly instead of quietly narrowing a search.

This endpoint is no longer reserved: decision **D-050** replaced the 501 with real self-service issuance, and I4 added the reversible `disable`/`enable` beside the one-way revoke. See the *Tenant: your own API keys* folder in the full collection.

The key this collection uses is an analyst key, which does not hold `apikey:manage` - issuing credentials is not part of running searches. So the refusal you get here is a permission one, and it is the correct one.

exec: pm.test('refused, because an analyst key does not manage keys', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.eql(403));
